en: Theragāthā 2.1 Dukanipāta, First Chapter The Elder’s Verses, Book Two, Chapter One, No. 1: The Pair of Verses on the Elder Nanda. 1. "I am not one who has gone forth for the sake of robes, nor for the sake of alms-food, nor for the sake of a bed and seat; I have gone forth out of faith, seeking the state of peace. 2. "For me, there is no delight in the household life, which is crowded with many cares; I shall wander alone like a rhinoceros, mindful and clearly comprehending."
“There is no state of existence that is permanent,
Those aggregates arise and pass away again and again;
having understood this danger, [one should practice].
I have no desire for existence;
having emerged from all sensual pleasures,
the destruction of the taints has been attained by me.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Uttara speak these verses.
